title: From Craig Bellamy Salary to Your Own: How to Convert Hourly to Annual Pay in Australia
description: Convert your hourly rate to annual salary using the 38-hour week, including tax and super. Compare with Craig Bellamy salary and national averages from the ABS.
salarySummary: Using the 38-hour week, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour equals $52,260 annually before tax and super.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week (usually 38 for full-time) and then by 52 weeks. For example, $30 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $59,280 gross per year. This assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime or penalty rates.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage is the legal minimum ($26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026), but most employees are covered by an award which sets higher minimum rates, penalty rates, and allowances. Check your award via the Fair Work Ombudsman pay guides to ensure you're paid correctly.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on top of my salary?
faqs.a: Superannuation guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your salary. For a $60,000 annual salary, super adds $7,200 per year, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. This is not deducted from your pay; it's an additional benefit.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Hourly to Annual Conversion

If you're paid by the hour or considering a salary offer, the basic formula is straightforward: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. This gives your gross annual pay before tax and super. For full-time work, the standard week is 38 hours, as set by the Fair Work Ombudsman. For example, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, which equals $1,004.90 per week and $52,260 per year (38 hours × 52 weeks). 

But your actual pay may differ. Award rates, casual loading, penalty rates, and allowances all affect the hourly figure. The formula assumes you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime. For part-time or casual roles, adjust the weekly hours accordingly. A fortnightly figure is simply weekly pay × 2, which can help when budgeting between pay cycles.

## The National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage is the legal floor for all employees not covered by an award or agreement. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour for full-time and part-time employees, and $33.05 per hour for casuals (including 25% casual loading). However, most workers are covered by a modern award that sets higher minimum rates for their industry or role. Award minimum wages increased by 4.75% from 1 July 2026. Always check your specific award using the [pay guides](/blog) on our site or the Fair Work Ombudsman's Pay and Conditions Tool.

Award rates often include penalty rates for weekends, public holidays, or late nights. These are not captured by the simple hourly-to-annual formula. If you regularly work unsocial hours, your annual pay could be significantly higher than the base rate suggests.

## Casual Loading and Superannuation

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. When using our [the timesheet](/), you can check a box to add 25% casual loading to your base rate. **Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading** – the tool adds it for you. For example, if your base award rate is $26.44, the casual rate becomes $33.05 per hour.

Superannuation is paid on top of your gross pay. The super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 (2026–27). If your annual salary is $80,000, your employer must contribute an extra $9,600 into your super fund. This is not deducted from your take-home pay; it's an additional benefit. Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

## Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your gross annual salary is not what you take home. The Australian Taxation Office withholds tax based on the 2026–27 resident tax rates: nil on the first $18,200, 15% on income up to $45,000, 30% up to $135,000, 37% up to $190,000, and 45% above that. Plus a 2% Medicare levy (using 2025–26 single reduction thresholds). Use the ATO's gross pay estimator to estimate your net pay. Our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page also provides estimates.

For a worker earning the National Minimum Wage of $52,260, the annual tax (including Medicare) would be approximately $6,867, leaving about $45,393 take-home pay. This is a rough estimate; individual circumstances vary.

## Comparing with Craig Bellamy Salary

Craig Bellamy, the legendary NRL coach, reportedly earns a salary well above the national average. While exact figures are not publicly confirmed, his annual pay is often cited in the millions. To put that in perspective, using the 38-hour week formula, a $1.5 million annual salary equates to roughly $759 per hour. That's over 28 times the National Minimum Wage. The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports that full-time adult average weekly ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 in May 2026, or about $108,352 per year. [reference tables](/data) Even a high-end executive salary like Craig Bellamy's is a reminder of the wide range of pay in Australia.

When you see a headline about "Craig Bellamy salary," you can now convert it to an hourly rate and compare it to your own. The same formula works for any salary: divide by 52 weeks, then by hours per week. For a 38-hour week, a $200,000 salary is about $101 per hour.

## Using Our Tools

Our [the timesheet](/) lets you enter your base hourly rate and add casual loading if applicable. It calculates your weekly, fortnightly, and annual gross pay, plus estimated tax and super. Remember the disclaimer: annual pay is hourly rate × hours per week × 52, assuming the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For award-specific rates, check the [pay guides](/blog). For historical data and comparisons, see our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page. Understanding your hourly rate in annual terms helps you negotiate salaries, budget, and plan for the future.
